reason: The cornea and lens both bend light, so putting them together seems like a useful start on focusing it.
expectation: I expect a focusing front with both clear parts; it may still need the iris to control incoming light.

alternatives.reason: Building the light-sensitive lining also matches a goal, but I want to start with focusing.

effect: The cornea and lens bend light toward the same area, so I can add the iris to finish the front.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the two clear parts focus light together.
reason: The iris has an opening that can narrow, so it seems useful for controlling how much light enters.
expectation: I expect the iris to join the focusing front and control the opening for light.

alternatives.reason: The light-sensitive lining is another goal, but I want to finish the eye front first.

effect: The eye front is complete: the iris controls incoming light while the cornea and lens focus it.
reaction: The separate jobs of the iris and clear parts make sense.
reason: The only offered combination joins light-sensitive cells to nerve cells, matching the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect a light-sensitive lining connected to fibres that can carry signals away.

effect: The light-sensitive lining is called the retina, and its nerve fibres form the optic nerve. Both eye parts are ready to join.
reaction: It helps to see how the fibres gather into one outgoing bundle.
reason: The only offered combination joins the focusing front to the sensing lining, matching the new goal.
expectation: I expect an eye cutaway with light focused onto the retina and signals leaving through the optic nerve.

effect: The completed eye shows how the focusing front and retina work together, with signals traveling toward the brain through the optic nerve.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate parts form a complete route from light to nerve signals.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the eye front and retina was most worthwhile because it brought focusing, sensing and the outgoing nerve together in one picture.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the iris was clear, but less engaging than the final assembly because its light-controlling job was already shown in its picture.

surprise.text: Seeing the nerve fibres gather into one bundle helped me understand what the optic nerve is.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the parts' pictures and goals gave each combination a purpose. The last two choices were the only combinations offered, though.

continue.text: I would probably continue: building the complete eye made me curious about how the brain uses its signals, although this chapter offered few choices after the start.
